evidence.r1: The route/status filter pills, search field and zoom cluster show blurred map through them in shot-fv-light/dark; the alerts sidebar and the selected-vehicle platter (shot-menu-light) are solid content panels with no map bleed-through.
evidence.r2: The three top pills and the zoom cluster occupy separate, non-overlapping regions; the vehicle platter (shot-menu-light) sits clear of the top bar.
evidence.r3: Four to five glass elements (route filter, status filter, search, zoom cluster, plus the platter when a vehicle is selected), each load-bearing, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r4: All floating pills show the same frosted, moderately tinted regular-glass look in both shot-fv-light and shot-fv-dark.
evidence.r5: No clear-variant glass appears anywhere on the map surface in either scheme.
evidence.r6: No pill shows a distinct saturated tint separate from its neutral grey/white fill in shot-fv-light or shot-fv-dark; there is no single emphasised primary action.
evidence.r7: Every pill shows blur and edge highlighting over the map lines in both schemes rather than a flat colour box.
evidence.r8: The filter pills, search field and zoom cluster are capsules; the alerts sidebar corners are a fixed radius, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r9: The highlighted 'Queue on Victoria Bridge' row in the sidebar sits inset from the sidebar's own corner radius without a pinched arc, shot-menu-light.
evidence.r10: The floating filter and search pills are capsules; the zoom control cluster is a dense set of icons housed in one capsule rather than individually bordered rectangles, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r11: Route filter, status filter and search are three separate glass groups across the top bar, at the three-group limit, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r12: The 'All routes' text toggle shares one glass pill with seven colour-coded route number badges that act as filter chips, mixing a text control with icon-style controls, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r13: Glass is applied to each pill's outer shape; the colour dots and labels sit on the one shared surface rather than being individually glassed, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r14: The route filter, status filter and search pills keep a clear gap between them rather than merging, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r15: shot-full-light differs from shot-fv-light only in live sim timestamps and vehicle positions, not scrolled content; the sidebar and map never show content scrolling beneath a bar in these captures, so no edge effect is demonstrated.
evidence.r16: Every pill sits over the textured street/harbour map, never a flat field, in both schemes.
evidence.r17: Only the map, not the alerts list or platter text, sits beneath the floating pills at rest; the sidebar itself is never covered by any glass element, shot-fv-light/dark.
evidence.r18: Dark pill text in light mode and light pill text in dark mode both read clearly against the frosted fill over the map, shot-fv-light/dark.
evidence.r19: shot-reduced only shows the transparency toggle switched on with pills turning solid; no increased-contrast or reduced-motion state is captured.
evidence.r20: The 315px-wide alerts sidebar occupies the full left edge of the window in shot-fv-light/dark, so the map content never reaches that edge; the sidebar sits beside the map rather than the map running full-bleed under a floating bar.
evidence.r21: The boundary between the sidebar and the map is a sharp vertical seam with no gradient or background extension in shot-fv-light/dark.
evidence.r22: The vehicle platter (shot-menu-light/dark) has no added dark scrim behind it; the rest of the map is unchanged from shot-fv.
evidence.r23: Only the platter's position near the selected bus icon (shot-menu-light) can be checked from stills, not morphing, materialisation or press feedback.
evidence.r24: The 'All routes' filter pill itself displays seven saturated route hues (blue, green, olive, purple, pink, cyan, magenta) as part of the control bar, not the map content layer, shot-fv-light.
evidence.r25: Pill text (black/white) does not closely match any single map hue it sits over in either scheme.
